title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continuing the discussion of how a section of type (1) can 'specialize' into one of type (2). S is a base (normal, a localization of an arithmetic scheme), X/S is a smooth compactification of U = X − T, and T is a divisor étale over S with sections g_i, here a fixed g_{i0}. Over the generic point K one has the fundamental extension 1 → π → E_{U_K} → E_K → 1 and its integral counterpart E_U → E_S.

One is given a rational section f of U over S, i.e. essentially a K-point of U. At a particular point s of codimension 1 in S it meets the cusp: as sections of X, g_i(s) = f(s). Then f_K gives a section E_K → E_{U_K}. Take the inertia group I_{s'} ⊂ E_K at a point s' above s and compose with E_{U_K} → E_U. Inertia then goes into π_1 (it dies in E_S), and even into the cuspidal inertia subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1)-like attached to the cusp g_i ('on l'a vu'). The point is that this homomorphism is NON-trivial, because the point degenerates into the cusp.

To analyse this one passes to the decomposition group N_{s'} (notations of exact sequence (7)). Grothendieck identifies N_{s'} with the π_1 of the 'punctured disc' (rondelle trouée) attached to the non-strict henselization Õ of O_{S,s}, i.e. N_{s'} ≅ Gal(K̄/K̃) = E_{K̃}. Better, geometrically, it is the π_1 of the bundle of punctured discs around the germ of the variety D = closure of s.

The next page continues: the sub-extension of N_{s'} by π inside E_{U_K} is E_{U_K̃}. It maps to E_U over E_Õ ≅ Gal(k̄/k), and the given section restricts to a section of this local extension.

Purpose: a local (henselian) study of a section coming from a rational point which reduces to a cusp. Such a section is locally 'cuspidal / tangential-like' at s, and this is the bridge between point-sections (type 1) and cuspidal/tangential sections (type 2).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The transcription '... soit une [nulle] triviale' is almost certainly 'soit non triviale' (nontrivial inertia action, since f meets the cusp at s). 'I' in 'section de T sur I' should be S.

ideas.what: A rational point specializing at a codimension-1 point s into a cusp g_i: the inertia I_s acts through the section into π_1, indeed into the cuspidal inertia L_i, and nontrivially.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of rational points to cusps; local cuspidal behaviour of sections (inertia mapping to cuspidal inertia)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian geometry; Nakamura, Tamagawa, Stix (Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups, LNM 2054)
ideas.where_published: Cuspidal/tangential sections are evoked in the Esquisse d'un programme and the Letter to Faltings (1983) without this local computation

ideas.what: Identification of the decomposition group N_{s'} with Gal of the fraction field of the non-strict henselization, viewed as π_1 of a 'punctured disc', or better of a bundle of punctured discs over the germ of D = closure of s.
ideas.modern_name: Henselian/local Galois group as π_1 of a punctured tubular neighbourhood (geometric picture of decomposition groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (SGA1 / SGA 7 style); topological analogy is folklore
ideas.where_published: Henselization and decomposition groups in EGA IV / SGA1; the 'punctured disc bundle' picture is not, as far as I know, in print

ideas.what: Restricting the extension E_{U_K} → E_K to the decomposition group gives the local extension E_{U_K̃} → E_K̃, mapping to E_U → E_Õ ≅ Gal(k̄/k), with the section restricting accordingly.
ideas.modern_name: Localization of sections of the fundamental exact sequence at a place
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (e.g. Stix's local-to-global treatment of sections)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a local mechanism by which a 'point-section' of type (1) specializes, at a codimension-1 point where the point meets a cusp, into a cuspidal (tangential-type) section of type (2), via the punctured-disc picture of the decomposition group. The full specialization theory sketched here is not developed on this page, and is not completed in print by him.
missed.quote: Je voudrais enfin comprendre encore comment une section ... du type (1) peut se 'spécialiser' en une type (2) ... le π_1 de la 'rondelle trouée' ... ou mieux, le π_1 du fibré en disques troués
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Specialization of sections in families and limits of point-sections to cuspidal packets is studied in modern section-conjecture work (Stix, Saïdi, Hoshi). This is an early sketch, but the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A historically nice early sketch of the local behaviour of sections when rational points degenerate into cusps, with a vivid 'bundle of punctured discs' picture. The content itself is standard in modern anabelian geometry.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'le compactifié lisse [situation] de U = X − T sur S, avec une g_i = g_{i0} section de T sur S' (not 'ramification modérée d'itération', and 'sur S' not 'sur I').
'section rationnelle f de U sur S, qui en un point particulier s de codimension 1 va coïncider avec g_i en tant que section de X' (not 'en 14 par section').
'de sorte que l'homomorphisme induit sur le groupe d'inertie I_{s'} ⊂ E_K' rather than 'de sorte que U ... induite'.
'(qui envoie en fait I_{s'} dans π_1, et même dans L_i, on l'a vu) soit non triviale' rather than '= dans ... soit une [nulle] triviale'.
'(cf suite exacte (7), dont on reprend les notations)'.
Last line: 'ou mieux, le π_1 du fibré en disques troués' (continued on the next page).
